name: PDCLib
listed_description: The Public Domain C Library. Implements most of C99 and some of (awesome-c list, Standard Libraries)
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The GitHub repo page and its Readme.txt, Notes.txt, Internals.txt and Quickstart.txt (CC0-1.0, 296 stars) carry no benchmarks; Notes.txt even says the default memcpy() copies char-wise, contrary to 'earlier claims of performance', and tells users to use compiler builtins through a platform overlay. The project site pdclib.e43.eu is blocked (EGRESS_BLOCKED); the code is built for standards compliance and portability, not speed. Directional statement only, and it concedes slowness.

name: plibsys
listed_description: Cross-platform system C library. Zero third-party dependencies, uses only native system calls (awesome-c, Frameworks)
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The README says only that several implementation models are used 'to achieve maximum native performance on each platform' (directional); the 33-page wiki is platform and build documentation without benchmarks; NEWS mentions a 'major performance improvement for shared memory buffer (#105)' with no numbers or baseline. A WebSearch for plibsys versus GLib found no third-party benchmark. The GLib or pthread baselines guessed for it are never measured against it.

name: pth
listed_description: Portable implementation for non-preemptive priority-based (awesome-c list, Concurrency and Parallelism; text truncated in the seed)
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. gnu.org, gnu.cs.utah.edu, usenix.org, static.usenix.org and opensource.apple.com all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the manual, README and Engelschall's USENIX 2000 paper ('Portable Multithreading: The Signal Stack Trick for User-Space Thread Creation') could not be opened; WebSearch snippets of two queries showed only the qualitative claim that user-space cooperative threads switch context more cheaply than kernel threads, with no numbers and no named baseline. No GitHub mirror with benchmarks was found. Directional claim only.

name: qlibc
listed_description: Simple and powerful library, designed as a replacement for GLib while focusing on being small and light (awesome-c, Frameworks)
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The README (BSD-2-Clause, 1.0k stars) has only an API list and a table of big-O characteristics of the Tree, Hash, Static Hash and List tables; the tests directory holds unit tests (qunit asserts), no timing benchmarks; the wolkykim.github.io docs are blocked and a WebSearch for qlibc versus GLib found no third-party benchmark. Claim is 'small and light', which is directional with no numbers.
